title: Alex Belsten’s model of unique hue perception featured in UC Berkeley News
summary: Work by postdoc Alex Belsten provides an account for why humans tend to see and name colors as a combination of four “pure” hues — red, yellow, green and blue – based on natural scene statistics.

title: Denis Kleyko wins SSF Future Research Leaders award
summary: Congratulations to Denis Kleyko (postdoc 2000-2022) for being awarded a Future Research Leaders grant from the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research.

title: Daniel Kunin joins Redwood Center as Miller Postdoctoral Fellow
summary: The Redwood Center is pleased to welcome Daniel Kunin as a new postdoctoral fellow.

title: Galen Chuang awarded NIH fellowship
summary: Galen Chuang was awarded the NIH Ruth L.

title: Chris Kymn graduates, receives Bearden Book Award for outstanding research
summary: Congratulations to Chris Kymn for receiving the Alan Bearden Book Award for Outstanding Research upon graduating from the Neuroscience PhD program!

title: Alex Belsten and Galen Chuang present at VSS
summary: Alex Belsten was selected for a talk at Vision Sciences Society ( VSS) in May: “Sparse coding of color in natural images replicates unique hues and universals in color naming” ( talk session).

title: Chris Kymn and Zeyu Yun present at ICLR 2025
summary: Redwood Center members Chris Kymn and Zeyu Yun presented their work at the 13th International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR) in Singapore.

title: Redwood Center attends COSYNE 2025
summary: Alex Belsten, Galen Chuang, Ankit Kumar, and Zeyu Yun presented posters at the 2025 Computational and Systems Neuroscience Conference (COSYNE) in Montreal, Canada.

title: Redwood members present at Neurips 2024
summary: Redwood Center members Chris Kymn, Zeyu Yun, Galen Chuang and Sonia Mazelet presented at the Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (Neurips) in Vancouver, Canada.

title: Jamie Simon graduates, wins departmental thesis award
summary: The Redwood Center is excited to announce the graduation of Ph.D. student Jamie Simon in December 2024.

title: Redwood attends SfN 2024
summary: Redwood Center members Christopher Kymn (Olshausen lab), Eduardo Sandoval (DeWeese lab) and Hadi Vafaii (Yates lab) presented posters at this year’s Society for Neuroscience (SfN) conference, held in Chicago, IL from October 5-9, 2024!

title: Anthony Thomas starts new faculty position at UC Davis
summary: We are excited to announce that Anthony Thomas is now an assistant professor at UC Davis! Anthony worked with Fritz Sommer as a postdoctoral researcher in the Redwood Center from 2023-2024.

title: Ankit Kumar graduates
summary: While at Redwood, Ankit worked on understanding sensorimotor brain dynamics from the perspective of control theory and connectomics using approaches borrowed from statistical physics.

title: Terence Tyson, Zeyu Yun and Yazhou Zhao present at VSS 2024
summary: Redwood Center members Terence Tyson, Zeyu Yun and Yazhou Zhao presented their work at the Vision Sciences Society (VSS) at Tempa, Florida.

title: Chris, Sonia and Annabel present at NICE 2024
summary: Redwood Center members Chris Kymn, Sonia Mazalet and Annabel Ng presented a full (20+5) minute talk at the 11th Annual Neuro-Inspired Computational Elements (NICE) workshop, held in San Diego, CA from April 23-25, 2024.

title: Redwood Center attends COSYNE 2024
summary: Chris Kymn —alongside Connor Bybee, Sonia Mazalet and Denis Klyko— presented a poster at the 2024 Computational and Systems Neuroscience (COSYNE) conference, held in Lisbon, Portugal from February 29-March 5.

title: Connor Bybee awarded Swartz Foundation fellowship
summary: Connor Bybee has been awarded the Swartz Foundation Fellowship for Theory in Neuroscience to support his postdoctoral work in the Redwood Center.

title: Olshausen lab awarded NSF Robust Intelligence grant
summary: Bruno Olshausen’s lab, together with Nina Miolane at UC Santa Barbara and Stella Yu at University of Michigan (pictured above), was awarded a grant from NSF’s Robust Intelligence program for their project, “Lie group representation…

title: Yubei Chen starts new faculty position at UC Davis
summary: We are proud to announce that Yubei Chen (PhD 2019) has joined UC Davis as Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering.

title: Redwood Center attends ICLR 2023
summary: Redwood Center members from Bruno Olshausen’s group —Sophia Sanborn, Christian Shewmake and Zeyu Yun— as well as Redwood alum Yubei Chen presented their work at the 11th International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR).

title: Ankit Kumar presents at COSYNE 2023
summary: Redwood Center graduate student Ankit Kumar, advised by Kris Bouchard, presented his work as a talk at this year’s COSYNE conference, located in Montréal, Canada from March 9-14.

title: Redwood selected for three full talks at NICE 2022
summary: Redwood Center members Connor Bybee, Denis Kleyko, and Chris Kymn presented full (20+5) minute talks at the 9th Annual Neuro-Inspired Computational Elements (NICE) workshop, held virtually from March 28-April 1, 2022.

title: Redwood Center attends COSYNE 2022
summary: Redwood Center members Andrew Ligeralde, Raymond Wang, Connor Bybee, and Alexander Belsten presented posters at the 2022 Computational and Systems Neuroscience Conference (COSYNE) in Lisbon, Portugal.

title: Sophia Sanborn graduates
summary: Redwood is delighted to announce the graduation of Sophia Sanborn! Using the language of group theory, Sophia employs computational principles to extract symmetries in signals that are useful for both biological and artificial agents.

title: Vasha DuTell graduates
summary: The Redwood Center is excited to announce that Ph.D. student Vasha DuTell has graduated! Vasha’s thesis work explored the spatiotemporal properties of retinal images during natural tasks while accounting for head and eye motion.

title: Three Ph.D. students win graduate fellowships
summary: We are delighted to announce that three of our students were recently awarded prestigious Ph.D. fellowships! Jamie Simon (DeWeese lab) was selected as a National Science Foundation (NSF) Graduate Research Fellow.

title: Resonator network papers in print
summary: An exciting new model of factorization in neural circuits, called resonator networks, has been published in the December issue of Neural Computation.

title: Sparse coding selectivity and robustness explored in new JOV paper
summary: Now out in the November issue of the Journal of Vision, a new paper by Redwood alum Dylan Paiton and collaborators investigates how competition through network interactions can lead to adversarial robustness and selectivity in sparse…

title: Louis Kang starts new faculty position at RIKEN
summary: We are proud to announce that Louis Kang has finished his Miller Fellowship at UC Berkeley and is now a principal investigator at RIKEN’s Center for Brain Science in Japan.

title: Retinal image motion paper published in Journal of Vision
summary: The retina samples visual scenes using an approach dramatically different from any camera humans have so far designed.

title: Michael Fang, Charles Frye, and Ryan Zarcone graduate from Berkeley and the Redwood Center
summary: Leaving the friendly confines of the Redwood Center for a truly strange wider world this semester are three PhD students we will all dearly miss.

title: Zarcone, Engel, and collaborators explore analog coding in emerging memory systems
summary: Writing in Nature’s Scientific Reports, Ryan Zarcone and Jesse Engel have recently published their work on techniques for analog coding in Phase Change Memory!

title: Orthogonal CNNs @ CVPR
summary: In collaboration with Jiayun Wang, Rudrais Chakraborty, and Stella Yu, Yubei Chen’s work on enforcing convolutional orthogonality in convolutional neural networks will be presented at CVPR in 3 weeks–see you in cyberspace!

title: Yubei Chen graduates
summary: The Redwood Center is proud to announce that Ph.D. student Yubei Chen has graduated (actually back in December) and has continued on as a postdoc, as he works on various unsupervised learning topics.

title: Denis Kleyko starts a postdoc at the Redwood Center
summary: We would like to announce that Denis Kleyko, a computer scientist hailing from Luleå University of Technology, has joined the Redwood Center to study cognitive computation and Vector Symbolic Architectures.

title: Five new PhD graduates!
summary: It is with great pleasure that we highlight our five (!!) newly-minted PhD graduates. Brian Cheung Brian’s thesis work focused on structures that emerge in neural networks during learning.

title: Preprints galore
summary: New work from the Redwood Center has recently been released in preprint form across a variety of different topics — we encourage you to check out the following preprints which are in various stages of submission: Robust computation with…

title: Eric Dodds graduates
summary: We would like to wish Eric Dodds a big congratulations on receiving his PhD! Eric’s thesis explored consequences of implementation in models of biological neural systems that process low-level sensory information.

title: New paper: The Sparse Manifold Transform (to appear in NIPS 2018)
summary: Sparse coding, manifold learning, and slow feature analysis are typically thought of as three distinct forms of unsupervised learning.

title: Alex Anderson graduates
summary: Congratulations to Alex Anderson for graduating with his Ph.D.!

title: Neha Wadia wins Google Ph.D. Fellowship
summary: We are pleased to announce that our very own Neha Wadia has been named a 2018 Google Ph.D. Fellow in Computational Neuroscience!

title: New work on information storage in Phase Change Memory (to appear in DCC 2018)
summary: We’ll be at DCC 2018 to present some of our current work on information storage in next-generation semiconductor devices – come say hi!

title: New year, new look
summary: Welcome to the brand new website of the Redwood Center for Theoretical Neuroscience! We hope you’ll take a look around, read some of the new information we’ve added, and check back periodically to see what’s going on around here.

title: Simons Institute Program Kicks Off
summary: The Simons Institute program on The Brain and Computation is starting this week with a week-long bootcamp that aims to acquaint program participants with key themes from neuroscience and theoretical computer science.

title: Redwood Center welcomes new postdoc Louis Kang
summary: There’s a new face at the Redwood Center this week and it belongs to Louis Kang, a Postdoctoral Scholar joining us from UPenn!
